items.previewSummary: Violent incidents occurred across Bangladesh, resulting in one death and multiple vehicles set ablaze overnight. Police reported that activists of the banned Awami League and its affiliates initiated crude bomb explosions at various locations. Hasina, living in exile since August 2024, faces serious legal charges upon her potential return.

items.previewSummary: India has condemned the actions of foreign content creators misrepresenting conditions in New Delhi with footage from Dhaka. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal expressed concern over the distorted portrayal of living conditions. Reports revealed Chinese livestreamers broadcasting from low-income neighborhoods while claiming they were in India's capital. Authorities have been urged to take action against those involved in these misleading activities.

items.previewSummary: Cricket is often described as a "numbers game", where records are constantly made and broken. Some players reach major milestones, while others surpass existing records through their performances with the bat and ball. However, the players featured in this article will always hold a special place in history. After all, no one else can ever play Bangladesh’s first-ever Test match! On this day (10 November) in 2000, Bangladesh played their first-ever Test match against India at the National Stadium. Let us take a look at where the 11 players who featured in that historic playing XI are now.

items.previewTitle: Chase: Warrican won us the series
items.previewSummary: SYLHET, Bangladesh (CMC): West Indies Test captain Roston Chase has credited his deputy, Jomel Warrican, as one of the main reasons behind his side’s success in the recently concluded two-match Test series against Bangladesh. The West Indies won the series 1-0 after the second Test at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium ended in a tame draw yesterday. Left-arm spinner Warrican was named Player of the Series after finishing with 16 wickets, the most by any player across the two matches.

The West Indies won the series 1-0 after the second Test at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium ended in a tame draw yesterday. Left-arm spinner Warrican was named Player of the Series after finishing with 16 wickets, the most by any player across the two matches.
